A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLKV work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. v1 Appendices A.1–A.4 match v2 Appendices A–D; the expanded material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression experiments on two reasoning models and four benchmarks, alongside head-masking, error-mode, and training-component analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds a third model, MMLU-Pro evaluations, inference measurements, and additional analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use frozen language models, mixed-attention gating, GRPO with L1 regularization, self-distillation sampling, adaptive penalty weighting, and top-k head selection for inference. The revised explanation introduces no new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds knowledge QA evaluations on MMLU-Pro Chemistry, Computer Science, Law, and Physics, substantially extending domain coverage beyond mathematical reasoning and Python programming. DeepScaleR training and the four original evaluation benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: H2O, R-KV, and DuoAttention remain the evaluated compression baselines, with full-cache and random-head controls retained where relevant. Appendix F compares budget settings of existing methods rather than introducing new comparison algorithms.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen-3-4B model configurations, sampling of up to 500 instances per MMLU-Pro subset, latency/throughput sweeps, and batch-size comparisons at similar memory usage. It also introduces baseline-correct error analyses and fixed-versus-dynamic budget tests. The original main evaluation already used dynamic budgets.

E4.justification: New analyses examine response lengths on mutually correct samples, full-cache output-length distributions, and sensitivity to fixed versus dynamic budgets. Head-sensitivity and error-mode analyses are expanded and refined. The three original training-component ablations remain in Figure 8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Results remain point estimates; the unchanged four GRPO samples per query concern training rather than evaluation uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive Qwen-3 and MMLU-Pro results and reports 1.09–1.21× end-to-end speedups using doubled RLKV batch sizes at similar peak memory. Among matched results, Llama GSM8K at 0.4 sparsity changes from 88.4% to 86.8%, below R-KV's 88.3% and DuoAttention's 87.1% (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 4).

T1.justification: The substantive mixed-attention, GRPO, advantage, and adaptive-penalty equations remain equivalent. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are introduced. The operational description of reasoning-critical heads clarifies the existing concept.

C1.justification: The central head-identification and 20–50% near-lossless cache-reduction claims remain. v2 adds an explicit end-to-end speedup contribution and knowledge-task applicability, while dropping v1's explicit contribution claim that reasoning heads are functionally distinct from retrieval heads.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning generation termination, response-length selection effects, and fixed-budget fairness. It acknowledges comparable reasoning/retrieval head sensitivity in Qwen-3 and specific error-pattern exceptions. Earlier explanations invoking noise from non-reasoning heads and more distributed Qwen-2.5 reasoning are removed.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the prompt template, top-p settings, exact Qwen-3 checkpoints, FSDP details, and per-model training costs. It also describes the efficiency measurement stack and updates the project-page link. Most original optimizer, hardware, and data-construction details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds sparse/gated-attention references and positioning, including Longformer, MoBA, Native Sparse Attention, and Gated Attention, plus Qwen3 and MMLU-Pro citations. The existing comparison with compression methods and RL-based efficiency research remains largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, terminology shifts to reasoning-critical heads, and analyses move into a standalone Section 5. Future Work is rewritten, appendices are reorganized into A–F, an Impact Statements section is added, and the LLM-use declaration is removed.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, expands Figure 5 from eight to 24 panels, adds a compression schematic and efficiency/length/budget displays, and enlarges model coverage in tables and heatmaps. Error plots also receive revised legends, scales, and baseline bounds.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens generalization evidence through a third model and four knowledge domains, while Table 2 supplies actual runtime and memory measurements beyond v1's cache-budget comparisons. Additional analyses and reproduction details further strengthen the empirical case. These gains outweigh reporting defects, including Appendix E's inconsistent 200/3019 percentage and Figure 6's reversed panel descriptions. The speedups specifically concern larger batches at similar memory usage.
